title: The Tennis Court Next Door

features.name: the net that learned to move
features.desc-on-touch: Where the rope should catch the ball, wind and sea-memory have made it shimmer instead. The mesh holds nothing now.

features.name: the boundary that became a reading
features.desc-on-touch: The chalk lines waver as if they are recording something the ground is saying. You stand inside and outside at once.

features.name: shelter from what weather
features.desc-on-touch: The small roof that was meant to shade watchers. Now it holds only static and salt and the smell of rust.

features.name: where someone sat and waited
features.desc-on-touch: The slats wear the grain of hands that never came back. Salt stain in the wood pattern spells a name you cannot quite read.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the court where you both forgot to play
narr: you stood at the baseline. she held the racquet
loosely, like she had never held one before.
the ball sat between you. you did not serve.
instead you both watched the sky press down—
the way the light came through the chain fence,
how the sea-salt static in the air made everything shimmer wrong.

inscription: I do not know if it is the court anyone meant to find next door
